strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#9587 (statsmodels PR#9909): multinomial_proportions_confint(method='sison-glaz') raises Exception "Couldn't find a value for 'c'" on sparse or small-n counts because the c-search starts at c=1 and nu(c) can plateau below 1-alpha. Build statsmodels from source at buggy commit 67ca8f98c1ed with the era-pinned stack, then run the five sison-glaz tests added by the PR (four sparse parametrized cases plus the R-reference case). They must error on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed one.

pip_packages: statsmodels==0.14.4 (documented; source checkout at 67ca8f98c1ed is what is built, so the released 0.14.4 wheel must NOT be used as the buggy revision)
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/statsmodels/statsmodels.git && cd statsmodels && git checkout 67ca8f98c1ed
python -m pip install numpy==2.0.2 scipy==1.15.3 pandas==2.2.2 patsy==1.0.1 cython==3.0.12 pytest==8.3.5
pinned_because: numpy 2.0.2: documented in issue#9587 show_versions output (explicit, numerically relevant)
scipy 1.15.3: documented in issue#9587 show_versions output (explicit, numerically relevant)

statsmodels 0.14.4: documented as the reporter's installed version; the build target is the buggy commit, not the release
era_ceiling is null for all packages, so no era-inferred ceiling is applied; all pins above are explicit, not inferred

strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision 67ca8f98c1ed: all 5 selected tests ERROR, because multinomial_proportions_confint raises Exception "Couldn't find a value for 'c'" inside the test body before any assertion runs. Fixed revision: all 5 selected tests PASS, with the shape, bounds [0,1], and point-estimate containment asserts holding for the sparse cases and the R-reference vector [1,1,0,0,0,0,0] matching [0.5,1.0],[0.5,1.0],[0,0.9655815875] x5 under assert_allclose atol=1e-6.

risks: Installing the released statsmodels 0.14.4 or a nightly wheel would not contain the buggy commit; the fix is only observable by building from source at 67ca8f98c1ed and then at the fixed commit.
The C/Cython extensions must be rebuilt against numpy 2.0.2 and scipy 1.15.3; a stale build from another numpy version can break import rather than reproduce the bug.

The evidence does not show any platform, architecture, sanitizer, or threading dependence; the failure is a pure Python-level search exception, so it is expected to transition on any x86_64 Linux build. No platform-specific behaviour is claimed, and none is assumed here.

The R reference value is 0.9655815875 in the test but 0.965582 in the rebase discussion; the difference (~1.8e-7) is inside atol=1e-6 but is small, so an alternate R version would still pass only narrowly.

The R-reference test relies on the judgment call that exact saturated-box coverage (1.0) replaces the approximation once c+1>=n; if the fixed revision handles this differently, the test values could move.
The R-reference vector is only valid where count+c never exceeds n; inputs outside this were not validated against R, so the fixed revision's behaviour there is not covered by the test.
Previously working inputs are claimed unchanged in the PR body but not measured in the evidence, so regressions outside these five tests are not checked by this plan.
Running with -k sison_glaz selects only the five target tests; the other proportion tests are not run, so unrelated regressions would go unnoticed.
Rebase discussion mentions a CI failure dated 2026-07-16 described as unrelated; no detail is given, so it is not used to decide the transition.
Python 3.11.13 is taken from the environment context; no evidence was given for other Python versions.

oracle.why: R's own implementation silently returns invalid intervals in the no-crossing case, so R is used as the reference only for the valid-crossing vector [1,1,0,0,0,0,0]; the sparse cases use property checks (bounds in [0,1], containment of point estimates) instead of a numeric oracle.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 67ca8f98c1ed the c-search starts at c=1; for these inputs nu(1) either already exceeds 1-alpha or nu(c) plateaus below it, so no crossing is found and the function raises Exception "Couldn't find a value for 'c'". Each of the five tests therefore ERRORs at the call, before any assert.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the search starts at c=0 with nu(0)=0, and exact coverage 1 replaces nu(c+1) once c+1>=n, so a solution is found. The sparse tests pass the shape, [0,1] bounds, and containment asserts; the R-reference test passes assert_allclose against the R values at atol=1e-6.
